answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may vote on shared work, with one vote per locked token and rewards weighted by time at risk. A sybil attacker can create endless accounts, but cannot multiply influence without acquiring and immobilizing more tokens; that capital has an opportunity cost and may be slashed if identities coordinate to approve fraud. A cipher can protect private ballots, while saffron-tagged audit records give honest agents an anchor for tracing suspicious clusters.
